qualityBar.verdict: Clear Sky clears the PlayBound Bar as the faction-war prequel that makes the Zone feel contested rather than empty, with a DRM-free GOG master easy to own without a mandatory launcher.

expected.longDescription:
Clear Sky is the middle chapter of the original S.T.A.L.K.E.R. trilogy in story order and the prequel in chronology. You play Scar, a mercenary hired by the Clear Sky faction after a Great Emission reshapes the Zone. Where Shadow of Chornobyl is a loner's path and Call of Pripyat is an officer's investigation, Clear Sky is about choosing sides while Duty, Freedom, bandits, and Clear Sky itself fight over the same roads, outposts, and artifact fields.

The shooting and anomaly systems sit between the first game and the finale: familiar detectors, radiation, bleeding, and inventory weight, with emissions that force everyone toward shelter and faction conflict that can close routes you thought you owned. Capture points and war progress make maps feel contested rather than empty between scripted missions.

GOG's DRM-free offline installer is the PlayBound master. Galaxy is optional. Clear Sky does not require owning Shadow of Chornobyl or Call of Pripyat — each trilogy game is its own purchase and folder. Community overhauls belong elsewhere; free-roam Anomaly and GAMMA live under the Anomaly catalog page, not as Clear Sky editions.

Expect classic Zone friction: old menus, stiff faces, and a learning curve that rewards listening before sprinting. It remains the best way to feel the Zone as a battlefield of ideologies instead of a scavenger's private sandbox.

qualityBar.verdict: The Zone becomes a tug-of-war: taking an outpost can make the road home more dangerous than the road in.

set.longDescription:
Clear Sky begins before Shadow of Chornobyl, when a massive Emission shakes the Zone and a mercenary named Scar survives something he should not. The Clear Sky faction wants to understand what happened; everyone else still wants the same roads, artifacts and ground. That gives the middle release of the original S.T.A.L.K.E.R. trilogy a different rhythm. Rather than moving through a landscape that seems to wait for you, you enter a territory where rival groups keep trying to change who owns it.

Faction War is the clearest expression of that idea. You can help one group take an outpost, then find that the front has shifted again by the time you return. A place that looked safe on the way out may be contested on the way back. It makes the Zone feel less like your private scavenging route and more like a bad argument conducted with rifles. The system can also be rough: an ally may not move when you want them to, and a campaign objective can feel less legible than the game expects. Clear Sky's ambition is easier to admire when you know it sometimes has sharp edges.

The shooting remains grounded in preparation. Radiation, bleeding, ammunition and inventory weight all matter. Anomalies punish the player who runs toward a promising artifact without checking the path first. Scar can improve weapons and armor through technicians, so the gear you keep becomes more personal than a disposable loot roll. Emissions give even a familiar route a reason to change pace: find shelter when the Zone tells you to, or stop worrying about the next faction fight.

GOG offers the commercial Windows game as a DRM-free purchase with an offline installer; Galaxy is optional. Clear Sky is standalone, so buying Shadow of Chornobyl is not a prerequisite. The store confirms single-player and multiplayer, and notes that a separate serial key may be needed for multiplayer. Steam also lists online and LAN PvP. Those are properties of the original game, while a PlayBound hosted dedicated server for this Draft entry has not been verified. We should not promise one until its server files and join path work end to end.

The current GOG requirements specify Windows 10, 2 GB RAM and 10 GB free disk space, with DirectX 9.0c-capable graphics. Those are install-space and compatibility figures, not a measured download size. Native controller support is not documented on the store pages, so keyboard and mouse are the reliable route until a PlayBound Controls profile has been tested.

We are reviewing Clear Sky because it makes the Zone a contested place. It keeps the trilogy's scavenging and unease, then asks what happens when every faction wants the same piece of land. The answer is often a firefight you did not plan for, and sometimes a road you thought you had already cleared.
set.thatOneThing: You help a faction seize the checkpoint, go artifact hunting, and return to find the road belongs to someone else.
